plain.text: Jesus told a story. A man planted a vineyard and rented it to tenants. At harvest time he sent servants to collect his share, but the tenants beat them, and even killed some. Last of all he sent his beloved son, thinking, "They will respect my son." But they killed him too. Jesus said the owner would come and give the vineyard to others. He quoted Scripture: "The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone." The leaders knew the story was about them. They wanted to arrest him but feared the crowd.

Some Pharisees and Herodians tried to trap Jesus: "Is it right to pay taxes to Caesar or not?" Jesus asked for a coin and said, "Whose image and inscription is this?" "Caesar's," they said. Jesus said, "Give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's." They were amazed.

Some Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, asked about a woman who married seven brothers in turn. Whose wife would she be in the resurrection? Jesus said they did not know the Scriptures or the power of God. In the resurrection, people do not marry, but are like angels. And God told Moses, "I am the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob." "He is not the God of the dead, but of the living."

A teacher of the law asked, "Which commandment is the most important?" Jesus answered, "Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one. Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, mind and strength. The second is this: Love your neighbour as yourself. There is no commandment greater than these." The man agreed. Jesus told him, "You are not far from the kingdom of God."
Teaching in the temple, Jesus asked how the teachers could say the Christ is the son of David, when David himself, inspired by the Holy Spirit, called him "Lord". The crowd listened with delight.

Jesus warned, "Watch out for the teachers of the law. They like to walk around in long robes, be greeted with respect and have the best seats. They take advantage of widows and make long prayers for show. They will be punished most severely."

Jesus sat watching people put money into the temple offering box. Many rich people gave large amounts. Then a poor widow put in two tiny coins. Jesus said, "This poor widow has put in more than all the others. They gave out of their wealth, but she, out of her poverty, put in everything she had to live on."

summary.bigIdea: Jesus faces hard questions in the temple and points to wholehearted love for God and neighbour.
points: The story of the vineyard warns the leaders who are rejecting God's Son.
The greatest commandments: love God with everything, and love your neighbour as yourself.
A poor widow's tiny gift is worth more than the rich people's large gifts.
summary.reflection: Jesus said to love God with all your heart, soul, mind and strength. Which of these is hardest for you?
